# Summary

The PopPK model has to reproduce the PBPK (PK-Sim) bioequivalence decision across the 27 release
formulations (Weibull dissolution T50 × shape). Twelve structural variants were tested in three rounds:

1. **Disposition and absorption structure** (M1 → M4, 2026-10-16 to 10-23): a gut absorption step
   between release and plasma (M3) cut the T/R Cmax GMR error from up to 20 % (M1) to ≤ 3.5 %.
2. **Delay-style `@delay` input** (M1d–M3d and no-lag variants, 10-24): with the release lag kept,
   `@delay` reproduces the ODE models exactly; without the lag, fits and curves are much worse.
3. **Fixing M3's early peak** (M3L, M3Lo, M5, M6, 10-24 to 10-25): a dual-Weibull release (M5) fits
   better on every arm and cuts the Tmax bias in half; estimating the lag or adding a transit chain does not.

**Final model: M5** (dual Weibull in the `@delay` form, fixed lag → ka → 2-compartment, fitted per arm).
**Fallback: M3.** Equations and Pumas code: `model_equations/felodipine_poppk_models.pdf`.

# Common set-up

| Item | Setting |
|---|---|
| Data | 27 PK-Sim arms × 100 subjects, 18 samples 0.5–96 h, 15 % proportional noise (seed 20261016); the same noisy dataset for every model |
| Dose, units | 10 mg = 26 024 nmol; h, L, nmol/L |
| Release lag | 0.3113 h, fixed (PK-Sim value) unless stated |
| IIV | Log-normal on release time, CL, Vc |
| Residual error | Proportional |
| Estimation | FOCE, Pumas, per arm; two starting points, the higher LL kept |
| Diagnostic arms | 4.78 h/0.764 (reference), 4.78/0.5, 4.78/1.5, 2.39/0.764, 9.56/0.764 |
| Benchmarks | Cmax and AUC vs PBPK in the same subjects; T/R Cmax GMR vs the reference arm; Tmax and mean curve vs noise-free PK-Sim; BE limits and Type I error (felo_02–04) |

# Round 1: disposition and absorption structure (2026-10-16 to 10-23)

**M1, 1-compartment + Weibull release.** The first production model, fitted on all 27 arms. It had two
likelihood basins, and in 23 of 27 arms the best fit was a fast "release" (implied T50 0.3–2.4 h) with a
very large Vc (≈ 4000 L) — release and distribution were not separated. Cmax/PBPK ranged 0.87–1.135
across arms, which biased the T/R Cmax GMR by up to 20 %. The PopPK safe space diverged from PBPK away
from the reference shape.

**M2, 2-compartment + Weibull release.** Q or Vp ran to their bounds from either start: the peripheral
compartment is not identified without an absorption step. Rejected.

**M3, Weibull release → first-order absorption (ka) → 2-compartment.** The gut compartment separates
release from appearance in plasma, giving PBPK's fast rise and plateau without forcing release to be fast.
On all 27 arms: AIC better than M1 on 27/27, Cmax/PBPK 0.976–1.043, GMR error ≤ 3.5 % (M1: 20 %).
Remaining problems: the fitted T50 is about twice PK-Sim's (≈ 9.4 h at the reference 4.78 h), Vc is
non-physiological on some arms (≈ 2500 L at shape 1.5), and the curve peaks 0.4–0.7 h early at shape ≥ 0.764.

**M4, M3 paired (reference and test in the same subjects, shared disposition).** Fitted to two arms at
once, with separate release parameters per period. Much worse than two separate M3 fits; several fits
produced non-finite predictions for up to 75 of 100 subjects, and the GMR error was −12 % to +15 %.
Reason: in the PBPK model the release rate changes where along the gut the drug is absorbed and so how much
gut-wall CYP3A4 extraction it sees, so disposition as seen from the gut is not shared across formulations.
Rejected.

# Round 2: delay-style `@delay` input (2026-10-24)

**Question.** Do the results stay the same if the hand-written Weibull hazard ODE is replaced by the Pumas built-in delay form (`@delay(Weibull(shape, scale), cmt)` with the dose at bioavailability 0)?

**What happened.**

- The first version had no lag, as in the plain `@delay` form. Fits were much worse (M3d0 reference LL −755 vs
  −354), M1/M2 peaked too early, and M3d0 overshot by 60 % at 0.5 h.
- Adding the lag inside `@delay` needed workarounds:
  - Pumas ignores `@dosecontrol` lags when `@delay` is used (identical output with and without).
  - `Tlag + Weibull` gives an infinite likelihood for shape < 1, as does a dose record placed at t = lag.
  - Working form: `@delay(Tlag + truncated(Weibull(γ, α), 1e-4, Inf), cmt)`. The truncation removes at most
    0.4 % of the release (shape 0.5), less than the 0.01 h clock floor already used in M3.
- **With the lag, M1d/M2d/M3d reproduce M1/M2/M3**: LLs within 3 units, identical Tmax and mean curves,
  same GMRs. Run times were similar to the ODE.

**Conclusion.** The `@delay` form is equivalent and was adopted for the new structures; the lag must stay.

# Round 3: fixing M3's early peak (2026-10-24 to 10-25)

**Diagnosis.** M3 rises correctly but peaks early and falls too fast, worst at shape 1.5 (Tmax 5.3 vs 6.0 h,
only 28 % of subjects within 0.5 h of PK-Sim). Two physiological explanations were checked first:

- *Regional gut-wall extraction varying with release rate*: rejected — AUC per fraction absorbed is flat
  within ±3 % across the 27 arms.
- *Deconvolution against PK-Sim's "absorbed into mucosa" output*: inconclusive (implied half-lives ≤ 2 h).

The remaining explanation is structural: one release timescale and one ka cannot give both the fast initial
phase and the long late tail. Four variants were tested on the diagnostic arms:

| Variant | Idea | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| M3L | Estimate the lag (`@delay`) | Infinite likelihood at the start on all 4 arms with shape < 1 (the lag derivative of the truncated density is singular); at shape 1.5 LL −224 vs −56 fixed |
| M3Lo | Estimate the lag (ODE) | Lag lands at 0.27–0.33 h on most fits (≈ the fixed 0.3113); LL worse than fixed on 4/5 arms; the second start ended far worse (LL −840 to −5650) on every arm |
| **M5** | **Two Weibull release components (FF mixture)** | **Best LL on all 5 arms (+7 to +97); Tmax bias −0.3 to +0.15 h; mean-curve error 1.2–4.6 %** |
| M6 | 3 transit compartments instead of ka | Fixes the shape-1.5 curve (LL +19) but no better than M3 elsewhere; 2 of 10 fits failed |

**Decision (2026-10-24):** M5 final, M3 fallback.

# M5 on all 27 arms (2026-10-24/25)

Fitted with `02c_fit_poppk_m5.jl` (results in `output_rich_m5/`), compared with M3 by `felo_09`.

| Measure | M3 (fallback) | M5 (final) |
|---|---|---|
| AIC better | 0 / 27 arms | **27 / 27** (median ΔAIC −48, range −289 to −6.5) |
| Cmax ratio PopPK/PBPK | 0.976–1.043 | **0.976–1.019** |
| AUC₀₋ₜ ratio PopPK/PBPK | 0.985–1.012 | **0.989–1.004** |
| Cmax T/R GMR error vs PBPK | max 3.5 %, mean 1.6 % | **max 3.3 %, mean 1.3 %** |
| Tmax bias (median of arms) | 0.45 h | **0.20 h** |
| Subjects with Tmax within 0.5 h | 64 % | **76 %** |
| 2-D safe-space T50 limits vs PBPK | mean \|Δ\| 0.08 h, bias +0.03 h | mean \|Δ\| 0.09 h, bias −0.09 h |

**Caveats.**

- The two release components describe the curve; they are not two physical processes (fast fraction
  0.02–0.97 across arms; on some arms component a is a 0.2–0.4 h burst).
- The mixture's 50 %-release time is ≈ 8–9 h at PK-Sim 4–5 h, the same offset as M3: the PopPK input lumps
  release, gut transit and absorption.
- At the reference arm the fast fraction (RSE 45 %) and Q, Vp (RSE 55–70 %) are poorly determined; Vc reaches
  ≈ 2300 L at shape 1.5, as in M3.
- One arm (6.31 h / 1.2) still peaks 0.85 h early.
- The 2-D safe-space limits sit slightly low because M5 overpredicts the reference-arm Cmax by 0.9 %, so its
  T/R GMRs run about 1.5 % low at shape ≥ 0.9.

# BE decision vs PBPK (felo_04, 2026-10-25)

**T50 axis (shape 0.764): limits where BE is lost (h).** Cmax sets every limit; AUC never reaches it.

| | Lower | Upper |
|---|---|---|
| PBPK | 3.25 | 6.96 |
| M3 | 3.40 (+0.14) | 6.83 (−0.13) |
| **M5** | **3.27 (+0.02)** | **6.86 (−0.10)** |

**Type I error** — chance of passing BE when the true (PBPK) product sits at the limit the PopPK model would
declare (nominal 5 %; 20 000 simulated trials, seed 1234):

| | M3 | M5 |
|---|---|---|
| Lower, Cmax, n = 24 / 54 | 7.6 % / 10.2 % | **5.3 % / 5.8 %** |
| Upper, Cmax, n = 24 / 54 | 5.8 % / 6.8 % | **5.6 % / 6.3 %** |
| Lower, joint, n = 24 / 54 | 5.8 % / 10.1 % | **4.0 % / 5.6 %** |
| Upper, joint, n = 24 / 54 | 4.6 % / 6.6 % | **4.4 % / 6.0 %** |

**Shape axis (T50 4.78 h).** PBPK loses BE at shape 1.465. Both PopPK models underpredict the shape-1.5 Cmax
GMR (M3 1.235, M5 1.227, PBPK 1.269), so neither reaches 1.25 within the tested range: both would call shapes
1.465–1.5 bioequivalent. Unchanged from M3: the TOST control (reference × 0.80) gives 4.7–5.1 %, and RSABE /
ABEL accept 20–22 % / 13–14 % at the ABE limit (n = 24).

**Noise check (10-25).** To see whether the shape-1.5 shortfall is noise, M5 was refitted on the reference,
shape 1.2 and shape 1.5 arms (T50 4.78 h) with two new residual-noise datasets (seeds 101 and 202):

| Cmax GMR vs reference (n = 100) | Shape 1.2 | Shape 1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| PBPK | 1.119 | 1.269 |
| M5, seed 20261016 (original) | 1.101 | 1.227 |
| M5, seed 101 | 1.136 | 1.242 |
| M5, seed 202 | 1.112 | 1.240 |

At shape 1.2 the seeds land on both sides of PBPK, so that gap is noise (about ±1.5 %). At shape 1.5 M5 is
2–3 % low and below 1.25 on every seed: the shortfall is structural. The fitted fast fraction at the reference
arm varied from 0.02 to 0.15 between seeds, so the two release components describe the curve rather than being
identified individually.

# Run notes

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 10-23 | A queued run never started: the `pgrep -f` waiter matched its own command line (~7.5 h lost). Waiters now use the PID or a sentinel file. |
| 10-24 | A finished M4 run looked hung: its wrapper was a zombie, which `kill -0` still reports as alive. |
| 10-24 | M2d0 at the reference arm (disposition start) hung > 40 min and was killed; recorded as skipped. |
| 10-24 | Pumas `@delay` lag limitations found (Round 2). |
| 10-24/25 | M5 27-arm run: two scripting bugs fixed in the first hour (arm ordering; loading saved fits needs the original module name). At ~58 min per arm with two starts, the run was switched to the absorption-limited start only — on the 7 arms fitted from both it was never worse. 27/27 arms fitted; about 11 h wall time. |
| 10-25 | Noise check (`scripts/run_m5_noise_replicates.sh`, seeds 101/202, 3 arms each): 6/6 fits converged, 10–29 min each, done 16:14 IST. |
